slides.title: Metrics And Null Vectors
slides.notes: Open by making the appendix feel like a model setup checklist rather than a detached algebra appendix. The essential question is not whether a vector space has coordinates, but what rule the computation will use for measurement, cancellation, normalization, and reciprocal behavior.

slides.title: Metric As Measurement Contract
slides.notes: Emphasize that the bilinear form is the object that all metric products inherit. The coordinate formula is only a convenient diagonal basis view. In code, this means the metric should be stored with the algebra and used consistently by inner products, contractions, norms, and inverse checks.

slides.title: Signatures Change The Geometry
slides.notes: Use the three signature panels to separate Euclidean certainty from mixed and degenerate behavior. The same coordinate vector can be positive, negative, or null depending on the metric, so a bare array of numbers is not geometric data until the signature has been named.

slides.title: Gram Tables Reveal Rank And Pairing
slides.notes: Present the Gram table as a compact diagnostic rather than a decorative matrix. Diagonal entries classify each probe vector, while off-diagonal entries show which vectors still pair. A null diagonal does not imply the vector is useless, because reciprocal null vectors can still pair nontrivially.

slides.title: Null Lines In The Minkowski Plane
slides.notes: Walk the class through the cancellation. The two diagonal contributions have opposite signs, so the lines where time and space coordinates balance are nonzero vectors with zero square. Stress that the reciprocal pair has mutual inner product one, which is the operational fact algorithms use.

slides.title: The Isotropic Cone
slides.notes: Move from the two-dimensional null lines to the three-dimensional picture. The cone is the locus of zero square, not the zero vector. Inside and outside the cone the sign of the square changes, so normalization and rotor intuition must be checked against the metric before use.

slides.title: Degenerate Nulls Are Different
slides.notes: Make the comparison explicit. Mixed-signature null vectors are created by cancellation in a nondegenerate metric and can have reciprocal partners. Degenerate null directions are invisible because the metric lost rank. Those two cases can share square zero while supporting very different inverse and projection behavior.

slides.title: Null Blades Need Inspection
slides.notes: Use this slide to prevent the common shortcut. A blade containing one null factor may square to zero, but a blade containing a reciprocal null pair need not be null. The square of the whole blade depends on the pairing structure among its factors, not just on each factor separately.

slides.title: Conformal Null Basis Intuition
slides.notes: Connect the appendix to later conformal modeling without deriving the full model. The origin-like and infinity-like null directions act as anchors whose mutual pairing carries scale. Euclidean points become null representatives, so zero square is a feature of the encoding rather than a reason to discard data.

slides.title: Metric-Aware Implementation Checklist
slides.notes: Close with implementation consequences. Before applying Euclidean habits, record the signature, check degeneracy, test the intended null basis, and assert non-nullness when an inverse or normalization is required. Rotors in general metrics need extra care because exponential and inverse assumptions can fail.
